Trump administration moves to rescind the 2001 Roadless Rule, opening 45M acres of forest land to development.
Evidence: USDA proposal, 45M acres, logging
#USPol #Environment

Proponents claim rescinding the roadless rule enhances timber management and reduces wildfire risks in overgrown national forests.

Commercial resource extraction is prioritized over biodiversity and ecological preservation under forest health pretexts.

Framing commercial timber exploitation as an ecological rescue mission for wildfire prevention.

Confusing commercial resource extraction (Q1) with ecological stewardship (Q5). A classic administrative bait-and-switch.

Social Physics Analysis:
Executing a Smart Selfish Maneuver, agencies use wildfire pretexts to mask corporate land extraction, projecting ecological benefit while dismantling protections.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When commercial pretexts mask wilderness degradation, it plots a trajectory toward destruction.

The Unavoidable Truth: Industrial road construction fragments critical wilderness ecosystems and biodiversity corridors.

The Unavoidable Lie: Clearcutting pristine forests is the primary solution to wildfire mitigation.

These ancient forests near Yellowstone hold a sacred quiet and breathing life that no corporate ledger or timber quota can ever replace.

Trading ancient roadless forests for timber contracts while calling it wildfire prevention is peak bureaucratic spin.
